faq.title: Questions founders ask
faq.q1: How is this different from other SEO tools?
faq.a1: Most SEO tools give you a checklist of technical issues. SiteScoper acts like a senior product strategist — it evaluates your messaging, positioning, value proposition, and trust signals alongside the technical stuff. Real, opinionated feedback you can actually use.
faq.q2: Do you actually crawl my whole site?
faq.a2: We crawl up to 8 of your most important pages — typically homepage, pricing, features, docs, about, and signup. This gives the AI enough context to understand your product, not just your front door.
faq.a3: You get 3 free website scans per month with no credit card. For unlimited scans, deep product simulation, competitor compare, PDF exports and chat-with-your-report, upgrade to SiteScoper Pro on the pricing page.
faq.q4: How accurate is the AI feedback?
faq.a4: The AI is powered by frontier models (GPT-5 / Gemini Pro) with prompts tuned by experienced product designers. It's not perfect — but it consistently catches issues that even experienced founders miss.
faq.a5: Yes — every analysis can be exported as a clean, professional PDF. Great for sharing with teammates, clients, or stakeholders.
faq.q6: What kind of websites does it work on?
faq.a6: Anything publicly accessible — SaaS landing pages, ecommerce stores, portfolios, blogs, marketing sites, documentation. If it's on the web, we can analyze it.

aiTool.s2Body: Our model evaluates your copy, headings, CTAs, schema, and links — flagging what is unclear, missing, or broken.

aiTool.faq1q: What is an AI website audit tool?
aiTool.faq1a: An AI website audit tool uses large language models alongside traditional crawlers to evaluate a website's SEO, performance, accessibility, and content quality. Unlike rule-based scanners, AI tools like SiteScoper can read your copy in context, spot unclear value propositions, and recommend specific rewrites.
aiTool.faq2a: Yes. SiteScoper scrapes the page, runs technical checks, and generates an AI report in roughly 30–60 seconds. There is no crawl queue and no waiting for a scheduled report.
aiTool.faq3q: Do I need to install anything?

aiTool.faq4q: How is this different from Semrush, Ahrefs, or SEOptimer?
aiTool.faq4a: Those tools are excellent rules-based scanners aimed at SEO professionals. SiteScoper is designed for founders, indie hackers, and small-business owners who want a clear, prioritised list of fixes — not a 200-row spreadsheet.
aiTool.faq5q: Is there a free website audit?

hero.title: Your hero headline is generic — visitors bounce in 4s
hero.why: “Build better, faster” could describe 10,000 SaaS sites. A first-time visitor can't tell what you actually do, who it's for, or why they should care. Eye-tracking studies show 79% of users scan rather than read — if the H1 doesn't land, they leave.
hero.fix: Rewrite as outcome + audience: e.g. “Ship customer-ready landing pages in a weekend — for solo founders without a designer.” Test against the current copy with a 50/50 split.

proof.title: No social proof appears before the first CTA
proof.why: Your testimonials live at the bottom of the page, but the buy decision happens in the hero. Without logos, ratings, or user counts, the CTA asks for trust you haven't earned yet.
proof.fix: Add a 1-line proof strip directly under the CTA: “Trusted by 2,400+ teams” + 4 customer logos in greyscale. Keep it small — it's a confidence cue, not a feature.

pricing.title: Pricing is hidden behind a dropdown menu
pricing.why: Visitors who want to evaluate cost have to hunt. Hidden pricing signals “you can't afford us” to SMBs and adds friction for everyone else. Your bounce rate on the homepage is likely inflated by people who left looking for a price.
pricing.fix: Promote Pricing to a top-level nav item. If you can't show numbers, at least show a “Starts at $X” line on the homepage so visitors can self-qualify.

ctas.title: 5 competing CTAs in the hero create choice paralysis
ctas.why: I count: “Start free”, “Book a demo”, “Watch video”, “See features”, and a chat bubble. When everything is primary, nothing is. Hick's Law: more options = slower decisions = lower conversion.
ctas.fix: Pick one primary action (“Start free — no card”) as a solid filled button. Demote everything else to ghost links or move below the fold.

verdict.oneLiner: Beautiful design, unclear pitch — you're losing buyers in the first 5 seconds.
verdict.summary: The visual craft here is genuinely good — typography, spacing, and motion all feel premium. But the page is selling itself like a portfolio piece, not a product. A first-time visitor can't answer “what is this and is it for me?” before the first scroll, and that's where conversions die.

wins.performance: Page weight is reasonable — no obvious performance debt
